rics.description: Commercial Banks, Performance, loan to deposits ratio (%)
rics.meaning: Loan-to-Deposit Ratio (LDR) for commercial banks — share of deposits being lent out. Indonesia regulatory norm is 78-92% (BI's macroprudential corridor).
rics.how_to_use: Above 92% requires extra reserve provisioning under BI's RIM (Reserve Requirement based on Intermediation) rules. Below 78% means banks are sitting on excess liquidity. Recent system LDR ~85-90%. Higher LDR = banks lending more aggressively; rising LDR with deposit outflows flags liquidity stress.

rics.description: Commercial and Rural Banks, claims on other sector, claims on other financial institutions
rics.meaning: Commercial and Rural Banks: Claims on Other Sector, Other Financial Corporations — bank loans to non-bank financial institutions (insurance, asset managers, finance companies).
rics.how_to_use: Tracks interconnections in financial system. Surge in claims on NBFIs may signal regulatory arbitrage or shadow-banking growth — OJK monitors.

rics.description: Commercial and Rural Banks, claims on other sector, claims on private sectors, loans
rics.meaning: Bank Claims on Local Government and State Enterprises — bank credit to public-sector entities (regional governments, SOEs like PLN, Pertamina, BUMN).
rics.how_to_use: State enterprises like PLN, Pertamina are major bank borrowers. Concentration risk: top SOEs hold significant share of bank loan books.

rics.description: Commercial and Rural Banks, claims on other sector, claims on public non financial
rics.meaning: Bank Claims on Non-Financial Corporations — corporate-sector lending. The 'real economy' bank credit channel.
rics.how_to_use: Cyclical with capex investment cycles. Watch for sector concentration (mining, real estate, manufacturing). High concentration in property/CRE is a vulnerability.

rics.description: Commercial and Rural Banks, claims on other sector, claims on state and local government
rics.meaning: Bank Claims on Households — consumer + mortgage lending. Same concept as aIDCRDCONAA at different aggregation.
rics.how_to_use: Track for household-leverage cycle. Indonesia household-credit-to-GDP ~17% — low but rising as financial inclusion deepens.

rics.description: Commercial and Rural Banks, net claims on central government
rics.meaning: Bank Net Claims on Central Government — banks' net position vs central government (gov bonds held minus government deposits).
rics.how_to_use: Indonesia banks are large SBN (gov bond) holders post-2020. Surge in net claims on government during easing cycles signals 'crowding-in' of bank balance sheets into Treasury bonds vs lending.

rics.description: Credit approval, consumer credits, total
rics.meaning: Consumer credit approvals — share of total credit approvals going to households (mortgages, vehicle loans, personal loans, credit cards).
rics.how_to_use: Track for household leverage cycle. Pre-2020 typically ~30-35% of total approvals. Surges during easing cycles when banks compete on consumer-loan rates. OJK monitors mortgage and auto-loan LTV (loan-to-value) caps for macroprudential signal — tight LTV slows this stat.

rics.description: Credit approval, total credits
rics.meaning: Total credit approvals — flow measure of new loan commitments by commercial banks. Leading indicator of stock-level outstanding credit.
rics.how_to_use: Approval flow leads outstanding-credit stock by 1-3 months (drawdowns lag commitments). Sharp slowdowns in approvals signal bank risk aversion or weak loan demand — early warning for deceleration in lending. Pair with consumer-credit-approval (aIDCRDAPPCC) for retail vs business breakdown.

rics.description: Credit of commercial banks to non bank third party, total
rics.meaning: Total Credit of Commercial Banks to Non-Bank Third Parties — the headline bank credit aggregate. Includes corporate, SME, and household lending across all currency denominations. Published monthly by Bank Indonesia.
rics.how_to_use: Indonesia bank credit growth typically runs 8-12% YoY in normal cycles. Sub-5% signals weak loan demand or tight credit supply (often during BI hike cycles); >15% suggests aggressive easing. Pair with M2 — when credit grows faster than M2, banks are funding loans by drawing down liquidity buffers.

rics.description: Credit of commercial banks to non bank third party, total, Chg Y/Y
rics.meaning: Total Bank Credit, year-over-year change — pace of credit creation by commercial banks to non-bank third parties. The most-watched bank-lending growth indicator.
rics.how_to_use: Tracks the credit cycle. >12% YoY = expansionary; <5% = stalling. Compare to nominal GDP growth — credit-to-GDP gap widening signals overheating; narrowing signals deleveraging. BI watches this for systemic-stability signals; OJK (banking regulator) targets specific sectoral exposures.

rics.description: Deposit Facility Rate
rics.meaning: Bank Indonesia Deposit Facility Rate — same conceptual measure as aIDRINTO in banking-data framing.
rics.how_to_use: Cross-check against aIDRINTO. The DF rate sets the floor of BI's interest rate corridor.

rics.description: Lending Facility Rate
rics.meaning: Bank Indonesia Lending Facility Rate — same conceptual measure as aIDRREPO in banking-data framing.
rics.how_to_use: Cross-check against aIDRREPO. The LF rate sets the ceiling of BI's interest rate corridor.

rics.description: Monetary Authority Balance, claims on banks, liquidity credit
rics.meaning: Monetary Authority Balance: Claims on Banks, Liquidity Credit — BI's lending to banks via repo and emergency facilities.
rics.how_to_use: Spikes during liquidity stress (2020 COVID). BI's term repo and FX swap operations show up here. Persistent large balance signals systemic dollar/IDR funding pressure.

rics.description: Outstanding credits of commercial banks, total
rics.meaning: Outstanding credits of commercial banks, total — stock measure of bank loan book. Different framing from aIDCBCRDTA but tracks the same underlying credit aggregate.
rics.how_to_use: Use either this or aIDCBCRDTA as the level measure; growth rates (aIDLONYAR) are the meaningful signal. Decompose by sector (working capital, investment, consumption) for cyclical decomposition — investment loans are the most rate-sensitive component.

rics.description: IFDI, Financial Performance, Islamic Banking, Assets
rics.meaning: Islamic Finance Development Indicator (IFDI): Financial Performance, Islamic Banking, Assets. Reference data on Indonesia's Islamic finance ecosystem (Sharia-compliant banking, takaful insurance, sukuk markets, Islamic funds).
rics.how_to_use: Indonesia is a major Islamic-finance market — ~7% of total banking assets are Sharia-compliant. The Financial Services Authority (OJK) targets growing this share. Reference indicator for tracking Islamic-finance ecosystem development; not a macro indicator.
